P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No exchange controls: they ended in December 1951 (Bank of Canada), and there are no restrictions on borrowing from abroad, repatriating capital or remitting income (Deloitte 2026). Receiving foreign payments is unrestricted; FINTRAC reporting applies to large transfers (not captured).

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Canadian banks offer personal U.S.-dollar accounts to residents. RBC's U.S. Personal Account is a U.S.-dollar account with chequing privileges, aimed at people who live in Canada (USD 3 monthly fee, 6 free debits). TD's Borderless Plan is a U.S. Dollar Account, and you can move money between your TD Canadian- and U.S.-dollar accounts online. Other currencies are less common at retail level (not researched).

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Canadian residents are taxed on worldwide income, with foreign tax credits. Residence depends on residential ties: a home, spouse and dependants. 2026 federal rates are 14% (lowest bracket, reduced from 15%) up to 33%, plus provincial/territorial tax. Self-employed people report business income and pay both shares of CPP (not captured).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Federal GST is 5%; harmonized HST applies in some provinces (rates not captured). Registration is required above CAD 30,000 of sales (small-supplier threshold). Most exports of goods and services are zero-rated, so services to foreign clients are generally GST-free. CRA rules: you are a small supplier while taxable supplies stay at or below CAD 30,000 over four consecutive calendar quarters. TRAP: a sole proprietor counts WORLDWIDE taxable supplies, including zero-rated ones, so income from foreign clients counts toward the CAD 30,000 even though it is generally GST-free. If you exceed CAD 30,000 in a single quarter, GST/HST applies from the supply that crossed it. If you exceed it over four quarters, you stop being a small supplier at the end of the month after that quarter.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: PIPEDA applies to private-sector organisations across Canada that collect, use or disclose personal information in the course of commercial activity. Organisations must follow its 10 fair information principles. Some provinces (Quebec, Alberta, BC) have their own substantially similar laws (not captured).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: none of the major platform barriers apply. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Physical or digital goods on Etsy (Etsy seller payments are available here). (6) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Fully localized'). (7) Stripe accepts merchants here, so you can take card payments directly on your own site. (8) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
